data.answer:
The fall mainly reflected applications being brought forward into 2013 ahead of the **Raising the Bar** reforms, rather than filed in 2014. The reforms raised the standard required for an invention to receive a patent, prompting a rush to file before their implementation in April 2013 and a subsequent drop in applications that carried into 2014.[1]

IP Australia received **25,947 standard patent applications in 2014, down 13 per cent from 2013**. The 2015 report attributed the decrease to the reforms, while the 2016 report noted that applications returned to their previous trend in 2015.[2]

citations.quote: The new law raised the standard required for an invention to be granted a patent. This led to a rush of applications and examination requests in the weeks leading up to the implementation dates, and a resulting drop in applications for the remainder of 2013 which carried over into 2014.
prior to the implementation of Raising the Bar in April 2013.
It can reasonably be assumed that the historically high number of applications in 2013 was caused by the early filing of applications which otherwise would have been filed in 2014.

claims.text: The reforms raised the patentability standard and prompted applications to be brought forward into 2013, contributing to fewer applications in 2014.

citations.quote: IP Australia received 25 947 standard patent applications in 2014, a decrease of 13 per cent relative to 2013.
The decrease in filings may be attributed to the effects of the IP Laws Amendment (Raising the Bar) Act 2012 that took force in 2013.
The 2015 data shows that applications have returned to the trend observed since 2010.
